help.body: 🤖 Fleet monitor Tap the buttons under this message. You don't need to type node names. /all overview, /nodes list, tap a machine for details. Lookup (commands still work) /go name one node /cpu /mem /disk /today /traffic /net /xray /uptime Add a name or all, e.g. /cpu all NIC occupancy (current throughput, no generated traffic) /net sg ~3s sample /net all Public speed test (download/upload via Cloudflare) /bw sg ~3s each way /bw sg 8 1–15s /bw all Latency by region (four fixed addresses) /rtt sg /rtt all Coverage (typed, to avoid mis-taps) /add hk cap=2T reset=27 /cap hk 500G /off hk hide for now /on hk /kick hk remove; needs /add to return Caps: 500G / 1T / 2T / unlimited. The daily summary still sends automatically. Optional services (hidden unless configured) /svc hk xray 443,2053 /svc hk nginx 80,443 /svc hk xray off The node probes those TCP ports locally. The name is yours to choose. Tap 「中文」 or 「English」 to switch language. If a monthly cap and a reset instant in the host timezone are set, usage alerts at 80% and public traffic is cut at 90% until reset.

security.action.high: Action: review sources and application logs first; restrict access after confirming abuse.
security.action.medium: Action: check whether sources are your clients or monitors; investigate continued repetition.
security.behavior.replay: Repeated handshakes with altered session parameters
security.behavior.delayed: Identical handshake seen again after a delay
security.behavior.non_tls: Repeated unusual access to a TLS port
security.behavior.syn: Many connections do not continue the TLS handshake
security.behavior.background: First packet lacks a complete TLS handshake
security.backfilled: Recovered record, counted by its actual observation time.
security.observed_window: Counts use actual observation time; background first packets are not risk alerts.
security.evidence.replay: Identical TLS handshakes repeated across connections
security.evidence.session: Only session parameters changed between repeated attempts
security.evidence.response: Different parameters produced different server responses
security.evidence.malformed: Malformed TLS records followed the server response
security.evidence.pattern: Payload structure matches a known probe sample
security.evidence.close: Connections closed similarly after unusual payloads
security.evidence.delayed: An identical handshake returned after a longer interval
security.evidence.non_tls: One source repeatedly sent non-TLS content to a TLS port
security.evidence.syn: Many connections from one source never sent a TLS handshake
security.evidence.background: A first packet alone is insufficient to classify a probe
security.ip.note: Location and ownership are estimates from IP databases and DNS, not confirmed operator identity.
